notice: All examples use invented sources and results. They are illustrations, not reports from Jasmine’s workplace or measured outcomes.
modelAgnosticNote: Use the AI tool approved for your work with supplied material. Wording and layout will vary by model; look for the evidence, uncertainty and review decisions shown here. Connections and recurring runs depend on your setup.
goal: Build a starting point for the next colleague.

supplied.label: [K1] Digest README · revision 4
supplied.text: The team digest collects items marked ready in the queue and sends one email to the subscribed team. Ask: when is the digest scheduled, and where should I begin if someone reports a missing email? The operations team owns investigations.

supplied.label: [K2] Supplied config and runbook excerpt · current repository snapshot
supplied.text: digest.schedule: weekdays at 09:00 UTC. Runbook: for a missing email, inspect the run record for the relevant date and its delivery result. A successful job run alone does not establish that a recipient received the email.

supplied.label: [K3] Onboarding notes · revision 1
supplied.text: The digest goes out at 10:00 UTC on weekdays. The deployment schedule and recipient delivery records are not included in this source pack.

steps.label: Choose the reader's questions
steps.description: Supply the three excerpts and ask for an entry point covering scheduling and missing-email investigations. Keep the source labels and versions attached.

steps.label: Build a referenced map
steps.description: Explain the supported flow, answer each question with references, and expose the schedule conflict and missing deployment evidence. Do not fill the gaps with assumed behavior.

steps.label: Resolve the consequential gap
steps.description: An operations reviewer checks the deployed schedule and the referenced runbook before deciding what should become shared documentation.

sections.label: System overview
sections.text: Ready queue items → digest job → email to the subscribed team. Operations owns investigations. This is the flow described by the supplied README, not a verified account of a live run. [K1]

sections.label: When does it run?
sections.text: The current repository excerpt configures weekdays at 09:00 UTC [K2]. Older onboarding notes say 10:00 UTC [K3]. Treat this as a source conflict: the actual deployed schedule has not been established.

sections.label: Where do I start with a missing email?
sections.text: Inspect the relevant dated run record and its delivery result. Do not equate a successful run with recipient receipt. [K2] No run or delivery records were supplied, so this draft cannot diagnose a specific missing email. [K3]

sections.label: Gaps and proposed entry point
sections.text: First resolve the deployed schedule before a colleague relies on a send time. Then add links to the run records and delivery evidence. Proposed documentation outline: purpose and owner; verified schedule; missing-email investigation; source versions and open questions. No shared source has been updated.

outputRequirements: Where do I start with a missing email?
review: Can the reviewer follow every reference and verify which schedule is deployed?
Could a new colleague find the next investigation step without reading an unsupported diagnosis?
